title: Honey, Lime and Mild Ancho Butter
description: A short lime and honey infusion gives this smooth finishing butter a bright flavor and gentle ancho warmth.

steps.title: Warm the lime and honey
steps.text: Combine {juice}, {zest} and {honey} in the HexClad. Stir over low heat for 45–60 seconds until fluid and fragrant.

steps.title: Strain the infusion
steps.text: Press the mixture through a fine sieve into a small bowl. Let it cool for about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Blend the spices
steps.text: Mash {ancho} and {paprika} into {butter} until no spice clumps remain.

steps.title: Whip in the lime
steps.text: Beat the cooled infusion into the seasoned butter a little at a time until smooth. Divide into two portions and chill covered.

steps.title: Melt into a moist side
steps.text: Stir a portion into warm sweet potato mash or fold it into hot corn gravy just before serving.

notes: Make ahead: Make the butter up to 3 days ahead and refrigerate in a small covered dish. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions for up to 1 month; the small amount of infusion mixes back in as the butter melts. Fridge reheat: Stir one chilled portion into hot, freshly cooked mash or gravy until melted. If using leftovers, reheat the dish to 165°F first. Freezer reheat: Thaw the covered butter in the refrigerator and use it in a hot dish as for chilled butter. Option A uses lime and mild ancho. For gentler Option B, use smooth pear puree in place of the juice, omit the zest and ancho, and use sweet unsmoked paprika. An unsalted plant-based butter works for dairy-free portions. Estimated nutrition per serving of the prepared condiment (1/2 of recipe): 108 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 1.8 g total carbohydrate, 11.6 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 2 mg sodium.

steps.title: Set up the cooking vessel
steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
